question: What protective effect is attributed to the prior practice even in the case of a bite from great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Even in that case, poison does not enter the body.
The negation applies despite the bite.
inference: As a result of the preceding practice, poison has no effect even if one is bitten by great serpents.
uncertainties: The causal link is presupposed from the sequence of verses rather than argued here.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
